name: Donington Park 1938
notes: Donington Park in Leicestershire, opened for motorcycles in 1931 and for cars two years later, and by the late thirties the only British circuit fit to hold a Grand Prix. Five kilometres of parkland roads with real gradient in them — Redgate, the plunge to Craner Curves, Starkey's, Coppice and the Melbourne Rise — run clockwise past the trees of the Hall estate. The 1938 Donington Grand Prix on 22 October, delayed from its original date by the Munich crisis, went to Tazio Nuvolari in an Auto Union Type D from Hermann Lang and Richard Seaman for Mercedes; a fifth running was planned for 1939 and lost to the war.
author: Jim Lloyd
